# iliad-122 (19.1–73) — review of units.json

Reviewer pass on `units.json` only (`gloss.json` not read). Two passes: pass 1 in the runbook's order (notes against the Greek, Greek to `l`, `l` to `i`, remembered English, quotation marks and `mark`, packet flags, speech continuity), pass 2 re-read every changed unit and re-ran the mechanical checks (the edited units' `t` unchanged and still reproducing the packet text, `l` line count equal to `t`, quotation marks balanced in both layers, `mark` on the first unit of each of the four speeches, `p` on the units at 1, 12, 28, 37, 40). No modern translation was opened or recalled. Edited in place by script; `t` untouched (asserted).

Severity: high = wrong sense or a false statement of grammar that misleads; medium = departure from a house rendering or the table, or an `l`/`i` fault; low = a note's wording or accuracy, a line division, a small cross-reference slip. Counts: 0 high, 9 medium, 18 low (27 changes).

## Findings considered and refused

- **ἄρειον (19.56) / ἀρείων (19.33) as "better".** Kept. The Odyssey table fixes ἄρειον "better" (23.286, γῆρας), which is binding for the Iliad; the Iliad rows that avoid it are 2.707 (ἀρείων of men's courage, "braver") and 4.407 (a wall, "stronger"), and neither fits "was this any better for the two of us" or a body kept firm "or even better". The shipped odyssey-028 (line 182) and odyssey-093 (line 184) also use "better" for it. Note now names the form and the contrast with "braver".
- **κέρδιον (19.63) as "better".** Kept. The table fixes κέρδιον "better" (Odyssey 10.153, 11.358; Iliad 5.201; shipped as “better” in iliad-016 line 41, iliad-105 line 652 and iliad-112 line 417). The note now says it is "better" in the sense of more to one's profit.
- **The dashes at 19.27 (parenthesis).** Kept. After δείδω μή the verbs are subjunctives; πέφαται is a perfect indicative and Patroclus is already dead, so it cannot be one of the feared things. The English sets it between dashes and the note says why. Only the verb ("killed", not "slain") was changed.
- **μενεαίνω "raged" vs table "eager".** Not refused: reversed (two units, three changes). The drafter's reason (ἔριδι and ἀσκελέως supply the feeling) is a reason to read "eager" with them, not to depart; the table rejected "raged" by name in 16.491, "eager" is shipped in three other units (and the known-forms entry for μενεήναμεν says "we were eager"), and the validator enforces the same Greek, the same English. If the project wants "rage" it should be changed in the table for all of them at once.
- **ἀσκελέως "stubbornly" (19.68).** Kept as the English, since no better word is known; the note now says the sense is uncertain (see changes). Declined the drafter's avoided list ("relentlessly" etc.) as equally guessed.
- **Line 19.35 (the metrical note).** Kept as written. By hand: μῆ-νιν-ἀ (– ⏑ ⏑) | πο-ει (– –) | πὼν-Ἀ-γα (– ⏑ ⏑) | μέμ-νο-νι (– ⏑ ⏑) | ποι-μέ-νι (– ⏑ ⏑) | λα-ῶν (– ×): sixteen syllables make six feet only if the short -πο- of ἀποειπών is counted long, in the longum of foot 2; with it short the line has a foot too few. The irregularity is real, and the one sentence in the note ("short syllable -πο- of ἀποειπών has to be counted long, as the longum of the second foot") says where. The scanner agrees (UNRESOLVED plus "metrical lengthening … [longum of foot 2]").
- **γόνυ κάμψειν (19.72).** Kept; the note's "usually understood as taking rest" and `i` "bend his knee" repeat the table's 7.118 row exactly.
- **ἔγχει (19.49), "a spear" in `l` vs "their spears" in `i`.** Kept. `l` follows the singular; `i` follows the note, which says one spear for each man.
- **δῖα θεάων "heavenly-one of goddesses" (19.6).** Kept; it is the table's `l` (5.381, 18.388).
- **"to your wits" in `i` at 19.29.** Kept as a free-layer rendering of μετὰ φρεσί; "wits" is the table's word (4.245) and the sense is not changed.
- **"Because Achilles had appeared…" (19.45–46).** Kept; the `l` and `i` of the repeated line are the published iliad-118 wording, and the note's remark that it was said of the Trojans there is true (18.246–247).
- **μενεπτόλεμος as "stock" (19.48).** Kept; "steadfast in battle" is the table's (Odyssey 3.442) and the note is accurate that it is a stock epithet, if not Diomedes' commonest.
- **19.55, 19.28, 19.7, 19.46, 19.65–66 (published lines).** Checked: 19.7 `l`/`i` match iliad-038 (with the speaker carried over in `l` as the packet allows); 19.28 and the 19.55 line match iliad-117 and iliad-001; 19.65–66 `t` ends περ, (the comma now in the source), and `l`/`i` are identical to iliad-117's unit; 19.1–2 matches the shipped 11.1–2 in the English of the second line.
- **Speech continuity.** iliad-121 ends with Thetis flying down from Olympus; no quotation is open at its end, and 19.1 begins a new book. The four speeches here (Thetis 8–11, Achilles 21–27, Thetis 29–36, Achilles 56–73) open and close on the correct units in both layers; the last closes the part.

## Pass 2 — gloss.json and new-renderings.md

Every novel entry was read against the line(s) it parses and against the entry-format rules (lemma as LSJ gives it, general to the form, typographic ’ only, under 230 characters, no line numbers, no "here", Homeric forms name the Attic equivalent, genuine homographs joined by " · "); the 49 novel forms are all present and none is missing from `novel-forms.json`; every known form was checked against the existing entry in `iliad-glossary.json` for coverage of its use here; the existing `__broaden__` entries were checked to begin with the old entry whole. Longest entry 172 characters. Counts: 0 high, 2 medium, 10 low (12 changes to gloss.json), plus 5 new broadenings and 1 repair.

`new-renderings.md` updated to match `units.json`: the μενεήναμεν · μενεαινέμεν row deleted; ἐκ δ’ αἰὼν πέφαται now "killed"; new χρώς "skin" / "flesh" row; ἐπιεικές `i`; ἀσκελέως row (uncertain sense, "to be eager"); ἀπομηνίσαντος row (note says ἀπο- uncertain); ἄρειον row ("braver" for courage only).
